takeaway: IMN Sunday regional keeps an unstable moist ITCZ pattern: Pacífico Norte afternoon isolated storms and possible coastal rains tonight, with Nicoya heat near 32°C (down from yesterday’s ~37°C). OT#45 was Saturday’s story (latest IMN aviso Sat 5:50 p.m.); no tropical cyclone near Costa Rica. Midweek ensemble means still lean Pacific SW moisture / flanking EPAC lows, but the quieter Wed signal pushes the elevated gyre watch later than yesterday’s Tue–Thu window — still a watch, not established.

periods.label: Days 1–3 (Sun–Tue)
periods.pattern: Today (IMN Pacífico Norte, valid Sun 20 Sep): morning partial cloud with rain possible south of the region; afternoon partially cloudy with isolated storms; evening partial–mostly cloudy with possible coastal rains. General commentary: ITCZ over the region favors rains through the day, with Pacific maritime storms early and afternoon Pacific-side storms starting in mountains then shifting coastward near nightfall. Nicoya max ~32.3°C / min ~22.9°C (Liberia ~36.3°C). Weekly text (17–23 Sep) still mentions OT#45 activating the ITCZ Sunday into early next week — treat the daily regional as authoritative for today. GFS 06Z / ECMWF 00Z / GEFS mean 06Z 24-h maps keep Nicoya mostly light–moderate (~0.1–0.75 in / 24 h) through Mon morning. Papagayo light (NHC).
periods.implications: Mornings remain the better outdoor window; plan around this afternoon–evening convective window along the Pacific side. Heat is less extreme than Saturday but still warm inland.
periods.confidence: High for no nearby TC and a continued shower/storm day under ITCZ influence (IMN + NHC). Moderate on exact Nosara storm timing/amounts (IMN wetter language vs light–moderate model maps).

periods.label: Days 4–7 (Wed–Sat)
periods.pattern: Wed (~23 Sep): GEFS mean 06Z f072 still shows light flow and a ridge/high over northern Central America rather than a closed CR gyre; EPS mean 00Z f072 has only light W–SW 850 flow. By ~Fri 25 (f120), GEFS/EPS/AIFS-ENS means show flanking EPAC lows (~1002–1006 hPa) and W–SW 850 flow over Nicoya — more supportive of Pacific-side moisture. 24-h Nicoya totals in means stay mostly light–moderate (~0.3–1.25 in); ECMWF deterministic 00Z can be locally wetter around Fri (~0.75–1.5 in) but its f120 850 field looks more easterly with deep EPAC lows well offshore — do not let one det frame dominate. Not locked as a multi-day temporal.
periods.implications: Keep late-day plans flexible mid-to-late week; treat any wetter stretch as afternoon cells plus possible SW moisture, not a guaranteed temporales.
periods.confidence: Moderate for continued shower chances and a moister Pacific-side flow signal later in the week; low–moderate for sustained temporales or a closed Central American gyre.

periods.label: Days 8–15
periods.pattern: IMN sub-seasonal (21 Sep–18 Oct) still keeps Pacífico Norte below normal (weekly Pac Norte roughly 5–90 mm) with stronger-than-usual trades limiting Pacific-side rain. CPC GTH text (updated 15 Sep; valid 23 Sep–6 Oct) favors below-average Caribbean rainfall weeks 2–3; EPAC genesis risk is coastal Mexico / open EPAC, not CR. GEFS mean into ~30 Sep keeps Nicoya light (~0.1–0.5 in / 24 h) without a local extreme bullseye. Single deterministic frames can still show a wetter day later — treat as scenario only.
periods.implications: No official signal for a prolonged flood-season spike on the Nicoya Pacific side; short heavy cells remain possible.
periods.confidence: Moderate for below-normal / no major local TC theme; low for day-by-day rain.

gyreWatch.possibleTiming: Roughly mid–late week (~Thu–Sat 24–27 Sep) if flanking EPAC lows and sustained Pacific SW low-level flow persist; Wed looks quieter than yesterday’s Tue–Thu emphasis
gyreWatch.supporting: GEFS mean 06Z f120 (~Fri 25) shows ~1006 hPa L south of Mexico with SW 850 flow over Nicoya; EPS mean 00Z f120 has ~1001 hPa EPAC L and S–SW flow over CR; AIFS-ENS 00Z f120 has ~1002 hPa EPAC L with SW Pacific-side flow; GFS deterministic 06Z f072–f120 also carries onshore SW 850 flow. Short-term IMN ITCZ language supports a wetter Pacific start to the week.
gyreWatch.conflicting: GEFS mean Wed (f072) still has light easterlies / northern-CA ridge rather than a closed gyre; ECMWF det f120 shows more easterly 850 flow locally with intense EPAC lows far offshore; ensemble-mean Nicoya precip stays light–moderate; NHC has no disturbance near Costa Rica (TS Odalys and EP99 are well west/NW of CR); IMN sub-seasonal still favors Pacific rainfall deficit. Ensemble means only — no member-count probabilities. One dramatic GFS/ECMWF frame does not establish a gyre.

whatChanged: OT#45 is now yesterday’s IMN aviso story (Sat 19 Sep updates); Sunday’s regional forecast is ITCZ residual rather than a fresh wave-crossing headline. Nicoya heat drops from ~37°C to ~32°C. Biggest model shift vs yesterday: the elevated SW-moisture / flanking-low signal in GEFS/EPS/AIFS-ENS means drifts later (clearer by ~Fri 25 than by Tue–Thu), and Wed looks quieter — gyre watch stays elevated but timing slips later. Papagayo remains light; NHC now has newly named TS Odalys far from CR plus high-chance EP99 south of Manzanillo.
practical: Best apparent outdoor windows: mornings Sun–Tue before convective peaks. Worth planning around: afternoon–evening storms today under ITCZ (IMN), still-warm Guanacaste inland heat (Liberia ~36°C; Nicoya ~32°C), and Papagayo N–NE ~10 kt becoming variable <5 kt today with seas ~3–5 ft, then W–NW Mon and a turn toward SW midweek (NHC OFFPZ8 PMZ113; Thu night S 15–20 kt). Latest IMN avisos are Sat OT#45 updates — no new Sunday aviso on the list collected this morning.
